newsitem.title: USA: Blue chips worry again about higher interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips worry again about higher interest rates.

text.p: Stock prices were mixed Tuesday as blue chips were rattled anew by fears that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates next week, but a rally in technology and tobacco shares helped cushion the fall.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was off 16.65 points at 5,872.55 after closing at record highs on Monday and Friday. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 14-8 on moderate volume of 260 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"We're just giving a wee bit of ground after a sharp move on the upside. All signs show the market is working higher but we have some weakness. There's the fear the Fed will move to raise interest rates," said Alan Ackerman, a market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.

The Nasdaq Composite index, which is laced with technology stocks, rose 5.45 to 1,199.41 after Intel Corp., the world's No. 1 computer chip maker, said its third-quarter earnings would be better than previously predicted.
"Intel is helping Nasdaq and tobacco stocks bore the banner," Ackerman said. "On balance we're seeing some rotation but of the giveback, it's nothing serious."

The blue-chip Dow index, which closed Monday at a record 5,889.20 after trading briefly above the 5,900 level for the first time, had benefited from economic reports that pointed to moderating economic growth and tame inflation in August.
The numbers had boosted hopes that the Fed would not raise interest rates at next Tuesday's meeting of its policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee.

But bonds took stocks lower after Reuters quoted an unidentified senior Fed official as saying that eight of the 12 district banks in the Federal Reserve System have requested a hike of one-half percentage point in the discount rate, the rate the Fed charges banks for direct loans.
The news sparked a jump in Treasury bonds, with the 30-year bond falling 20/32 and its yield rising to 7.00 percent from 6.95 percent at Monday's close.
Technology stocks were bolstered by Intel's surprise announcement that its third-quarter revenues were running better than expected.
Intel rose 5 to 93-3/4 after touching a 52-week high of 94-5/8. Micron added 3/4 to 26-1/2, Compaq surged 2 to 63-3/8, ThreeCom was up 2-1/8 to 54-3/8 and Microsoft rose 2-5/16 to 133-13/16.
"The Intel news was very positive and is carrying the group," said Alice Hook, a trader at McDonald & Co.

Tobacco stocks rose after a Florida judge dismissed pre-1994 claims in a Medicaid lawsuit brought against the industry by the state of Florida. Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles said the key points in the lawsuit remained intact.
Philip Morris added 1-7/8 to 93-7/8, RJR Nabisco was up 1/2 to 27 and smokeless tobacco maker, UST Inc. rose 1-1/2 to 31-1/8.
